title: Never Straight? Equilibrium Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A lamp hangs still, a tug of war rope stops dead, a bridge holds up a bus. Big forces act on all three, so why does nothing move? And why can Aarav never pull the rope holding his bag perfectly straight, however hard he pulls? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn equilibrium of forces: a body is in equilibrium when the net force on it is zero.

On a live motion notebook a 2 kg bag hangs from two strings while the angle drops from 60 to 5 degrees. The readout and a tension vs angle graph move together: 11.3 N, 19.6 N, 56.4 N, then over 112 N. A slow-mo replay splits each tension into parts: the sideways parts cancel, the tiny upward parts must still hold the weight. We derive sum Fx = 0, sum Fy = 0 and T = W / (2 sin theta) step by step, see why two forces must be equal and opposite and three forces must close into a triangle, compare moving in equilibrium with being at rest but not in equilibrium, work through a lamp on two wires at 30 and 60 degrees, see the exam trap, and solve an original JEE Main pattern question.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A rope that never goes straight
0:25 What equilibrium means: net force zero
0:52 Motion notebook: two strings, one bag
1:18 Slow-mo replay: split each tension
1:32 The rule: T = W / (2 sin theta), step by step
2:13 Why the rope can never go flat
2:35 Two forces vs three forces + pause and think
3:09 Moving in equilibrium vs at rest + pause and think
3:45 Worked example: a lamp on two wires
4:23 Exam trap: each string does not hold W/2
4:44 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:25 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Contact and Non-Contact Forces. A magnet pulls a pin without touching it. How can a force cross empty space?
